vintage: BEA GDP by industry: historical 1947-1997 (Nov-16-2021 release), integrated industry accounts 1997-2023 (Sept-2024), annual 2017-2024 (Sept-25-2025), quarterly through 2026Q1 (Jun-2026); all before the Sept-30-2026 annual update, which raised 2025 GDP to $30,861.3B (+0.3%) and is not reflected. NIPA 1.10 (GDI, labor share), 6.16D corporate profits (Apr-9-2026), 2024 Use table (Sept-2025), FTE 2024 (NIPA 6.5D). Companies: fiscal 2025 results, market caps Sept-2026. Overlays: calendar 2025 and guidance to Jul-2026. Built 2026-10-01.
sources: BEA, Value Added by Industry 1947-1997, historical NAICS-based GDP by industry, release Nov 16 2021 (research/rc_gdpind_1947.csv; mirror https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcberg/macroeconomics/main/data/raw/gdp-industry-1947-1997.csv)

BEA, Integrated industry-level production account (KLEMS format): Components of value added by industry 1963-1997 and 1997-2023 (research/rc_klems63.csv, rc_klems-industry-1997-2023.csv; mirror https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rcberg/macroeconomics/main/data/raw/klems-industry-1997-2023.csv)

BEA, GDP by Industry: Value Added by Industry 2017-2024, Sept 25 2025 annual update (research industries.json valueAddedByIndustry; mirror https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahmdtrdi/P02-CreditScoring/main/data/01-raw/BEA_GDP_2017-2024.csv)

BEA, GDP by Industry, quarterly value added and real value added by industry through 2026Q1 (Jun 2026 release), via the US-chartbook data mirror (gdpva_nom.csv, gdpva_real.csv, ngdp.csv, gdp.csv; snapshot Sept 13 2026)

BEA, NIPA Table 1.1.5 GDP and 1.10 GDI by type of income (research/gdpgdi.csv, mirror https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IsaiahDal/isaiahdal.github.io/main/DATA/GDPGDI.csv; research/t11000.csv quarterly 1947-2024)
BEA, GDP and real GDP (chained 2017 dollars) 1929-2023, via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datasets/gdp-us/main/data/year.csv (implicit price deflator)

BEA, NIPA Table 6.16D Corporate profits by industry, Apr 9 2026 vintage (mirror https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ki3n98/AIS_datathon_2026/main/data/cleaned/corporate_profit_by_industry.csv)
BEA, NIPA Table 6.5D Full-time equivalent employees by industry 2024 (FRED series A4302C0A173NBEA, N43xxC0A173NBEA; search-verified)

Company filings FY2025 and market capitalizations Sept 2026 (research flows.json topCompaniesBySector, magnificent7)
IAB/PwC Internet Advertising Revenue Report, full year 2025 (Apr 2026); Meta, Alphabet, Amazon FY2025 results
Hyperscaler capex 2025 and 2026 guidance, Nvidia FY2026-FY2027 results, OpenAI and Anthropic revenue run rates (company releases and press via search; research industries.json aiOverlay)
Labor share: BEA NIPA 1.10 compensation of employees / gross domestic income 1947-2024, via research ownership.json factorIncomeShares_1947_2024

notes.gdp: Nominal GDP, $B, BEA (pre-Sept-30-2026 vintage; 2025 = 30762.1). 2026 is an estimate: 2025 x (H1-2026 / H1-2025) of quarterly nominal GDP SAAR (32175.9 / 30263.9) = 32705.5. The post-update vintage puts 2025 at 30,861.3 and H1-2026 at 31,906.3 / 32,563.0.
notes.deflator: GDP implicit price deflator rebased to 2025 = 100: BEA nominal / chained-2017-dollar GDP (datasets/gdp-us, Sept-2024 vintage) for 1946-2016, linked at 2017 to the Jun-2026 vintage quarterly data for 2017-2025 (2025 real growth 2.1%); 2026 = 2025 x the H1-2026 / H1-2025 implicit deflator, with real Q2-2026 from the 1.5% SAAR second estimate.
notes.laborShare: Compensation of employees paid / gross domestic income, NIPA 1.10 (annual averages of quarters; research ownership.json factorIncomeShares_1947_2024). 2025 = 2024 x the change in compensation / GDP (51.37% -> 51.18%) because 2025 GDI is not in the research.
notes.valueAdded: Industry value added sums to GDP every year (BEA value added by industry is additive in current dollars); differences are rounding only. Pre-1963 detail and pre-2017 software/print publishing splits are estimates; see each industry note.
notes.shares: compShare, taxShare: 2024 BEA Use table (trade: 2025 estimate including tariffs). depShare: estimated (no BEA depreciation by industry in the research); private depShares are scaled so that sum(depShare x 2024 value added) equals NIPA private consumption of fixed capital 2024 ($4006B); government uses general government gross operating surplus (= CFC). Owners keep 1 - compShare - taxShare - depShare. gosShare2024 = gross operating surplus / value added (2024).
notes.employment: Full-time-equivalent employees, thousands (BEA NIPA 6.5D for 2024). Earlier years convert BLS payroll jobs to FTE with each industry's 2024 FTE/jobs ratio, so they understate past full-time work slightly; 1950 and 1970 splits inside SIC divisions are approximate (+-15%). Excludes the self-employed.

corrections: Verification 2026-10-01: federal and state_local value added 1947-1962 re-split (totals unchanged). The logit split on the federal share of government purchases made state & local value added fall from $16.3B (1950) to $15.6B (1952) and then jump 19% in 1954, because Korean War equipment purchases lifted the federal share of purchases. State & local is now its 1963 ratio (0.716) to state & local consumption and investment (NIPA 1.1.5), federal the rest: 1947 23.4/10.1, 1950 20.6/15.1, 1952 33.2/17.7, 1955 35.0/22.9, 1962 50.4/39.2 (was 20.4/13.1, 19.4/16.3, 35.3/15.6, 36.0/21.9, 51.2/38.4). Notes updated.

Verification 2026-10-01: state_local blurb said it employs more people than any industry except health care, but in this file trade (19,668) and professional (17,424) have more FTEs than state_local (17,369). Reworded to 17.4 million FTEs, nearly one in eight US employees.
Verification 2026-10-01: mining_metals profitMargin 0.141 -> 0.14 (the stated blend 0.53 x 23.15% + 0.47 x 3.73% = 14.0%).

Verification 2026-10-01: software and real_estate notes called 2025 values BEA detail; the software-publisher share (85.9%) and the owner-occupied imputed rent ($2236B) for 2025 are the 2024 within-group shares applied to 2025 totals (research basis_2025). Notes reworded; numbers unchanged.

industries.note: Value added: BEA GDP by industry (historical 1947-1996, integrated accounts 1997-2016, annual 2017-2024, four-quarter average 2025). 1947-1962: BEA historical tables give only total government (GDP minus private industries); state & local value added is estimated as state & local consumption expenditures and gross investment (NIPA 1.1.5) x their 1963 ratio (0.716; the ratio stays between 0.71 and 0.73 through 1969), and federal is the rest. This keeps state & local growing through the Korean War, when federal purchases of equipment surged without adding much federal value added. 2026 (estimate): the industry's share of GDP in 2026Q1 (BEA quarterly value added, SAAR; 3.51%) x the 2026 GDP estimate, +3.6% on 2025. compShare from the 2024 Use table (compensation incl. government enterprises); depShare = general government's gross operating surplus, which the NIPAs set equal to its consumption of fixed capital; taxShare 0: enterprises' net subsidies (-6.8 $B) are netted against their small operating surplus. profitMargin: non-market (no profit). corporateProfits: none (government). Employment: FTE thousands; 2024 BEA NIPA 6.5D (civilian + military); 1950-2010 = CES federal jobs incl. Postal Service + DoD active-duty strength (recalled).

industries.note: Value added: BEA GDP by industry (historical 1947-1996, integrated accounts 1997-2016, annual 2017-2024, four-quarter average 2025). 1947-1962: BEA historical tables give only total government (GDP minus private industries); state & local value added is estimated as state & local consumption expenditures and gross investment (NIPA 1.1.5) x their 1963 ratio (0.716; the ratio stays between 0.71 and 0.73 through 1969), and federal is the rest.
